docs.title: 4D-Bio
docs.text:
4D-Bio is a community-maintained map of the skills needed to practice AI-assissted bioinformatics responsibly and effectively. It organizes key bioinformatics skills, derived from the ISCB Competency Framework v3.0 and selected publications, around four AI-fluency capabilities from Anthropic's 4D framework for AI fluency: Delegation, Description, Discernment, and Diligence.

Read the map

docs.title: The four capabilities
docs.text: Capability Anthropic's definition Meaning in bioinformatics Delegation Setting goals and deciding whether, when, and how to engage with AI Breaking complex problems into small independent tasks and determining the best bioinformatics tools to use for each. Description Effectively describing goals to prompt useful AI behaviors and outputs. communicating goals, context, and biological assumptions to AI agents in the form of technical specifications. Discernment Accurately assessing the usefulness of AI outputs and behaviors Using deep biological intuition to identify mistakes in AI-assisted analyses. Diligence Taking responsibility for what we do with AI and how we use it. Assuming accountability for the impact of agentic AI solutions on the global life sciences community.

docs.title: Who this is for
docs.text:
• Practicing bioinformaticians: self-assess where your AI skills are strong or thin.
  • Educators and curriculum designers: decide what to teach and how to train the next generation.
  • Team leads and hiring managers: write job descriptions and AI-use guidelines grounded in a shared vocabulary.

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text:
1. Read the Overview to see how the model is built and how its source frameworks fit together.
  2. Pick a capability and read its practice areas.
  3. Think about how each practice area connects to your daily activites and see what skills could help you.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text:
4D-Bio is an early draft and a call to the bioinformatics community. As domain experts, it is on us to decide how generative AI enters our daily work and our training programs.

See the How to contribute page for every way to help, from fixing a typo to proposing new additions. Use the pencil icon at the top-right of any page to propose changes.

docs.title: Our pledge
docs.text: We as members, contributors, and leaders pledge to make participation in our community a harassment-free experience for everyone, regardless of age, body size, disability, ethnicity, sex characteristics, gender identity and expression, level of experience, education, socio-economic status, nationality, personal appearance, race, religion, or sexual identity and orientation.

docs.title: Our standards
docs.text: Examples of behavior that contributes to a positive environment include: - Using welcoming and inclusive language. - Being respectful of differing viewpoints and experiences. - Gracefully accepting constructive criticism. - Focusing on what is best for the community. - Showing empathy towards other community members.

docs.title: Contributing to 4D-Bio
docs.text:
Corrections and new ideas are both welcome. Here is how you can help.

  • Community discussions: join the conversation on our Discussions page.
  • Reporting issues: if you found something wrong, open an issue and let us know.
  • Proposing edits: click the edit pencil icon on any page. It takes you to GitHub's web editor; when you save, you open a pull request.

docs.title: How to participate in the discussions
docs.text:
The Discussions page has two sections: the community forum and the general-purpose section. The community forum exists to become a shared knowledge base, so that informal conversations and individual actions reach more people. Sharing your experience there helps others more than you might expect.

  • AI Errors Archive: document cases where AI failed and how you caught the mistake.
  • Future of Bioinformatics: share what you do and do not want the future of AI-augmented bioinformatics to look like.
  • Model Feedback: share how the practice model helped you build or improve something, such as a workshop or a course curriculum.

docs.title: How to contribute to the practice model
docs.text:
To propose edits to the practice model directly:

  1. Fork the repo, or click the edit pencil in your browser.
  2. Make your changes in a new branch.
  3. Open a pull request against the main branch.
  4. Wait for review. A maintainer checks your changes for accuracy and fit with the practice model.
  5. Get credited. Once merged, the all-contributors bot adds your profile to our contributors page.

docs.title: For maintainers
docs.text:
The contributors page is kept up to date by the all-contributors bot. To credit someone, comment @all-contributors please add @username for content, ideas on any issue or pull request. The full workflow, contribution types, and fallback steps are in the maintainer guide.

This project is released with a Code of conduct. By taking part, you agree to its terms.

docs.title: Delegation
docs.text:
Delegation is "setting goals and deciding whether, when, and how to engage with AI" (Anthropic's 4D Framework for AI fluency). In bioinformatics, this requires a deep understanding of the biological context, breaking complex problems into small independent tasks, determining for which tasks it's appropriate to use generative AI, choosing the most appropriate AI-based or non-AI-based tool for each task, and knowing how to implement agentic workflows following best practices.

Practice areas on this page

  1. Framing the biological problem and formulating the solution roadmap
  2. Deconstructing the solution roadmap into actionable tasks
  3. Orchestrating autonomous AI workflows to execute tasks at scale

In the tables below, the Source column shows where each competency comes from: ISCB and ACTIVE competencies are drawn from existing frameworks; 4D-Bio competencies are original to this practice model.

docs.title: 1. Framing the biological problem and formulating the solution roadmap
docs.text: Category Competency Source Hypothesis generation Leverage domain expertise to formulate novel biological hypotheses and questions in research areas where existing data or AI training models are limited. 4D-Bio Innovative problem solving Devise alternative strategies or creative workarounds when standard computational approaches or AI models fail to solve a complex biological problem. 4D-Bio Workflow architecture selection Select the most effective combination of traditional bioinformatics tools and AI models to solve a specific biological problem. 4D-Bio Cross-disciplinary integration Incorporate multidisciplinary context and biological constraints to define the boundaries of a given computational solution. 4D-Bio

docs.title: 2. Deconstructing the solution roadmap into actionable tasks
docs.text: Category Competency Source Modular task decomposition Break down a complex bioinformatics problem into clear, individual tasks that can be performed independently. 4D-Bio Technical acceptance criteria definition Define the exact expected outputs, data formats, and quality benchmarks for each task before starting execution. 4D-Bio Awareness and Task-AI Alignment Critically assess the complexity of a task to determine if AI integration is appropriate or if it risks bypassing essential learning. ACTIVE Data Science Domain Knowledge D3: Use data science methods suitable for the size and complexity of the data. ISCB F3: Make appropriate use of bioinformatics tools and resources. ISCB

docs.title: 3. Orchestrating autonomous AI workflows to execute tasks at scale
docs.text: Category Competency Source Multi-agent architecture design Architect end-to-end automated workflows that leverage chained AI agents to execute complex, multi-stage bioinformatics analyses. 4D-Bio Human-in-the-loop checkpoints Engineer programmatic checkpoints and strategic pause points within automated workflows to surface high-stakes AI decisions for human validation. 4D-Bio Computational resource management Manage computational resources, API limits, and token budgets to keep automated workflows running efficiently. 4D-Bio Computer Science Domain H3: Make appropriate and efficient use of scripting and programming languages. ISCB Transparent integration Maintain "human-in-the-loop" governance for all computational conclusions. ACTIVE

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Description is "effectively describing goals to prompt useful AI behaviors and outputs" (Anthropic's 4D Framework for AI fluency). In bioinformatics, it requires communicating goals, context, and biological assumptions to AI agents in the form of technical specifications that drive the expected behaviors and make outputs reproducible and interpretable.

Practice areas on this page

  1. Translating biological knowledge into precise AI instructions
  2. Structuring raw biological data for AI model context
  3. Documenting and tracking AI interactions and software parameters for reproducibility

In the tables below, the Source column shows where each competency comes from: ISCB and ACTIVE competencies are drawn from existing frameworks; 4D-Bio competencies are original to this practice model.

docs.title: 1. Translating biological knowledge into precise AI instructions
docs.text: Category Competency Source Bioscience domain knowledge A3: Work at depth in at least one technical area aligned with the life sciences. ISCB Domain knowledge translation Translate deep domain-specific biological mechanisms, technical terminology, and experimental variables into precise computational instructions for AI execution. 4D-Bio High-context prompting Write structured, unambiguous prompts using advanced techniques to guide AI analysis. 4D-Bio Handle prompts as one more scientific resource that needs to be tested, documented, reported, reproduced, and cited. 4D-Bio Adaptive instruction Redirect AI systems dynamically when they drift from the expected analytical path or task boundaries. 4D-Bio

docs.title: 2. Structuring raw biological data for AI model context
docs.text: Category Competency Source Metadata standardization Apply highly descriptive system instructions that translate experimental designs and dataset annotations into clear parameters for AI ingestion. 4D-Bio Bioscience domain knowledge B3: Prepare life science data for computational analysis. ISCB

docs.title: 3. Documenting and tracking AI interactions and software parameters for reproducibility
docs.text: Category Competency Source Provenance logging Record every prompt text, system configuration, model version, and seed value used to achieve a computational result. 4D-Bio Automated documentation Generate exhaustive documentation that describes the functions, parameters, and expected outputs of AI-assisted code. 4D-Bio Version control Track changes to scripts, prompts, and configurations regularly using version control systems like GitHub. 4D-Bio

docs.title: Diligence
docs.text:
Diligence is "taking responsibility for what we do with AI and how we use it" (Anthropic's 4D Framework for AI fluency). In bioinformatics, it means assuming accountability for the impact of agentic AI solutions. This is not only about adhering to international standards for ethical and safe AI use, but also maintaining the cognitive abilities to remain critical of AI-generated outputs and complete tasks manually when AI agents fail.

Practice areas on this page

  1. Ensuring pipeline governance and regulatory compliance
  2. Securing digital asset longevity and sustainability
  3. Countering mental dependency while preserving technical mastery
  4. Nurturing a supportive and responsible scientific community
  5. Guiding institutional strategy and cross-sector diplomacy
  6. Elevating workforce capacity and educational legacy

In the tables below, the Source column shows where each competency comes from: ISCB and ACTIVE competencies are drawn from existing frameworks; 4D-Bio competencies are original to this practice model.

docs.title: 1. Ensuring pipeline governance and regulatory compliance
docs.text: Category Competency Source Professional Conduct J3: Comply with professional, ethical, legal, and social standards. ISCB AI regulatory alignment Monitor rapidly shifting regional and global AI legal frameworks to dynamically align pipeline deployments with local jurisdiction mandates. 4D-Bio Ethical evaluation Identify algorithmic bias and ensure that AI-driven decisions are calibrated, safe, and legally compliant. 4D-Bio Formulate institutional/team risk guardrails to prevent algorithmic discrimination, dual-use biological research hazards, or intellectual property infringements. 4D-Bio

docs.title: 2. Securing digital asset longevity and sustainability
docs.text: Category Competency Source Data Science Domain Knowledge E3: Manage own and others' data according to community standards (FAIR principles). ISCB Computer Science Domain Knowledge I3: Construct and maintain bioinformatics computing infrastructure. ISCB G3: Contribute to the design of user-centric bioinformatics tools. ISCB

docs.title: 3. Countering mental dependency while preserving technical mastery
docs.text: Category Competency Source Iterative skill development Counter "cognitive offloading" (the habit of delegating reasoning to tools) by intentionally practicing the "cognitive musculature" of manual coding and statistical reasoning. ACTIVE Professional Conduct M3: Engage in continuing professional development. ISCB

docs.title: 4. Nurturing a supportive and responsible scientific community
docs.text: Category Competency Source Professional Conduct L3: Work effectively in teams to accomplish common goals. ISCB K3: Communicate meaningfully with a range of audiences. ISCB Bioscience Domain Knowledge C3: Have a positive impact on scientific discovery through bioinformatics. ISCB

docs.title: 5. Guiding institutional strategy and cross-sector diplomacy
docs.text: Category Competency Source Visionary stewardship Design long-term technical roadmaps, governance models, and sustainability plans to secure the permanent operational longevity of bioinformatics initiatives. 4D-Bio Scientific diplomacy Navigate complex negotiations and communicate impact across academia, industry, and government sectors to align competing interests and influence decision makers. 4D-Bio

docs.title: 6. Elevating workforce capacity and educational legacy
docs.text: Category Competency Source Generational mentorship Develop early-career talent by actively mentoring them to leverage generative AI systems appropriately, critically, and responsibly. 4D-Bio Pedagogical dissemination Design open-access learning resources that leverage cloud and AI technologies to democratize access to scientific discoveries and dismantle structural educational inequities. 4D-Bio

docs.title: Discernment
docs.text:
Discernment is "accurately assessing the usefulness of AI outputs and behaviors" (Anthropic's 4D Framework for AI fluency). In bioinformatics, it means using deep biological intuition to identify mistakes in AI-augmented analyses, and using community standards to assess performance and confidence. It is also about calibrating one's belief in AI outputs against reference knowledge to ensure biological plausibility and statistical validity.

Practice areas on this page

  1. Evaluating the biological plausibility of AI outputs
  2. Benchmarking AI results against standard baselines
  3. Detecting computational artifacts and hallucinations

In the tables below, the Source column shows where each competency comes from: ISCB and ACTIVE competencies are drawn from existing frameworks; 4D-Bio competencies are original to this practice model.

docs.title: 1. Evaluating the biological plausibility of AI outputs
docs.text: Category Competency Source Biological integrity verification Verify the biological plausibility of AI-generated results against established mechanistic principles in your specific life science domain, and trusted reference sources or databases. 4D-Bio Critical Verification Protocols Implement structured validation procedures to audit AI-generated code. ACTIVE Statistical auditing Assess the statistical assumptions, significance estimates, and error measurements of AI-generated results to verify mathematical rigor. 4D-Bio Biological interpretation and contextualization Synthesize AI-generated results with established knowledge to extract meaningful biological insights and draw valid conclusions. 4D-Bio

docs.title: 2. Benchmarking AI results against standard baselines
docs.text: Category Competency Source Algorithmic bias detection Screen AI outputs for population skews, data imbalances, or training data biases across diverse experimental groups. 4D-Bio Automated evaluation design Build programmatic evaluation pipelines that automatically calculate error rates and compare AI outputs against gold-standard biological datasets or software tools. 4D-Bio Verification Confidence Calibration Close the "proof-belief gap" by aligning one's belief in an AI solution's correctness with objective accuracy outcomes. ACTIVE

docs.title: 3. Detecting computational artifacts and hallucinations
docs.text: Category Competency Source Hallucination detection Identify fabricated data, non-existent literature citations, or flawed logical loops within AI text and code outputs. 4D-Bio Collaborative code review Engage in structured peer code reviews, pull requests, and issue tracking on GitHub to systematically verify the accuracy and logic of AI-generated code in an iterative manner throughout the project's lifecycle. 4D-Bio Code auditing and debugging Audit AI-generated scripts line-by-line to expose syntax errors, silent logical bugs, or hardcoded variables before running them. 4D-Bio

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The model

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: 4D-Bio maps the day-to-day skills of a practicing bioinformatician onto a single framework for working with generative AI. This page explains how the model is built and how to read the four capability pages.

docs.title: How the model is built
docs.text:
4D-Bio combines three existing frameworks:

Framework What it contributes Anthropic's 4D framework for AI fluency The top-level structure: four capabilities (Delegation, Description, Discernment, Diligence) that together describe fluent, responsible AI use. ISCB Competency Framework v3.0 The established, profession-wide bioinformatics competencies. 4D-Bio links each practice area to the specific ISCB competencies it draws on, so nothing is invented from scratch. ACTIVE Framework AI-specific pedagogy: guidance on task-AI alignment, verification confidence, and countering cognitive offloading.

The 4D framework gives the shape, ISCB grounds the model in the wider profession, and ACTIVE adds the teaching-and-learning perspective for AI.

docs.title: How to read a capability page
docs.text:
The four pages (Delegation, Description, Discernment, and Diligence) are organized the same way:

  • A short definition of the capability, in general terms and then for bioinformatics.
  • A "Practice areas on this page" box listing the capability's numbered practice areas: the professional situations where it shows up in real work.
  • One table per practice area. Each row is a competency, grouped by category in the first column, with a Source tag in the last column.

docs.title: Source tags
docs.text:
The tag in the Source column shows where each competency comes from:

Tag Meaning ISCB Drawn from the ISCB Competency Framework v3.0. The tag links to the competency's ISCB entry. ACTIVE Drawn from the ACTIVE framework for AI pedagogy. 4D-Bio Original to this practice model, and not yet catalogued in an external framework.

docs.title: The four capabilities at a glance
docs.text: Capability Core question Focus Delegation Should AI do this, and how? Framing the problem, decomposing it into tasks, choosing tools, orchestrating agentic workflows. Description Did I communicate the goal well enough to reproduce it? Translating biology into precise instructions, structuring data as context, logging provenance. Discernment Can I trust this output? Judging biological plausibility, benchmarking against baselines, catching hallucinations and artifacts. Diligence Did I do it correctly? Governance and compliance, data longevity, preserving manual skill, mentoring and community stewardship.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: 4D-Bio is an early public draft (v0.1). Content, structure, and terminology are all still open for discussion. See How to contribute.
